A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KDM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, checkerboard simulations, ablations, scaling analyses, and a human evaluation with 300 decisions.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, loss-weight sensitivity experiments, and training-stability analysis.

M1.justification: The encoder–Koopman-operator–decoder architecture, reconstruction/latent/prediction/adversarial objectives, conditioning mechanism, KDM-F factorization, and training/sampling algorithms remain unchanged. The added weight sweeps test the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use checkerboard data, unconditional and conditional CIFAR-10, and unconditional FFHQ and AFHQv2 at 64×64. The human evaluation and qualitative test scenarios are retained; new comparisons and sensitivity analyses introduce no additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds offline IMM and 2-rf++ without pre-training, while retaining the original 2-rf++ comparison and removing StyleGAN2 and KD rows. Table 5 adds GET with adversarial training, replacing v1's unsuccessful comparison attempt. These additions substantially strengthen the relevant offline comparator set.

E3.justification: New experiments specify teacher-data-only IMM/2-rf++ comparisons, adversarial-weight sweeps, and loss monitoring excluding corrupted initial logs. Existing 50k-sample FID/IS evaluation and stated training budgets remain. Appendix D.1 calls 0.25 the default adversarial weight, conflicting with 0.01 retained in Section 4 and Table 7, so an actual main-experiment setting change is unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a completed GET-plus-adversarial control, sensitivity to Koopman-loss weights and adversarial strength, and generator/discriminator convergence analysis in new Figure 6. Section 5 adds an empirical spectral-norm check. These address attribution and stability questions beyond the retained loss-component and matrix-size ablations.

E5.justification: V3 newly reports the Koopman spectral norm as 0.88 ± 0.18, but does not define the dispersion measure or aggregation procedure. Neither version supplies benchmark confidence intervals or repeated-run counts; the new checklist's statistical-significance assertion adds no such details.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes KDM(EDM) FID/IS from 4.97/9.22 to 4.65/9.21, reversing its FID ranking against unchanged KDM-F at 4.68. New results include IMM at 4.81/9.16, offline 2-rf++ at 6.32/9.01, GET+Adv at 6.13/8.98, and sensitivity/convergence findings. Most existing results remain; unexplained setting differences prevent treating the KDM update as an established same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1–5.2, their assumptions and proofs in Appendices A–B, and Appendix C's factorization derivation are retained. The inverse-flow notation in Section 4 clarifies the same noise-to-image mapping. The added spectral-norm measurement supplies empirical interpretation rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: V3 narrows the headline from consistent state-of-the-art offline performance to competitive performance and removes the headline 40% improvement statement. Section 6.2 explicitly identifies GET as the comparator for percentage improvements. The central single-step Koopman-distillation and semantic-preservation contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit discussion of offline generation/storage costs, expressivity and adaptability constraints, and cost amortization in Appendix E.5. It interprets the new analyses as supporting stable optimization, weight robustness, and practical bound tightness. Existing outlier explanations and broader applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 newly states that all runs use a single A6000 or RTX4090 and notes distributed-training support. Removing the failed GET-adversarial discussion also removes its 120-hour KDM and 480-hour GET estimates. Most implementation and access information remains, while the conflicting adversarial-weight descriptions introduce reproducibility ambiguity.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations on privacy, time-series generation, operator modeling, IMM, and concurrent Koopman-based generative-flow work by Turan et al. Section 2 acknowledges that concurrent work and removes the explicit first-use claim. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, offline-versus-online discussion, and experimental narrative. V3 adds a NeurIPS checklist and appendix subsections on stability and cost, while retaining the overall section structure and most existing prose, proofs, and algorithms.

P2.justification: V3 adds the convergence plot in Figure 6, revises Table 1's rows, and extends Table 5 with GET+Adv. Existing qualitative figures are retained and renumbered/reflowed; Table 4 moves, and author formatting and citation coloring change. The visual presentation is locally revised rather than comprehensively redesigned.

improvement.justification: The completed GET-plus-adversarial control addresses a comparison v1 explicitly could not complete, while newer offline baselines and stability analyses strengthen the empirical case. Narrower claims and clearer cost tradeoffs also help. These gains are limited by conflicting adversarial-weight defaults and unreconciled KDM scores between Table 1 and the retained full-loss ablation, leaving important reproducibility questions.
